report.summary: Planning critique of rounds 16–18 for the PHAROS_INC and AgentReceipt comparison, judged only on deterministic checks and clear reports (PHAROS) and evidence-linked replayable receipts (AgentReceipt). The direction is sound: server-owned typed evidenceNeed metadata, a namespaced manual-review channel, and exact-version negative tests target the cited gaps. However, the plan as written does not pin down how export and verification handle the new optional fields. Current strict-key validation (evidence-export.ts:176, :184 and the item loop that does not read new keys) would reject or ignore new assessment metadata, so round 17's export and replay evidence would not be reproducible. Input validation of the new server metadata is unspecified, so a forged or model-supplied reason could pass. Source-file targets and 1000-unit feedback drafts also lack rules that make their truncation and target messages truthful. Failing to bind risk status back to the item and to record every suppression as an auditable event would make the AgentReceipt-style receipt weaker than promised. All findings below are design risks from an unexecuted paper review; no runtime behavior or tests were run.

findings.title: Round 16/17 optional assessment metadata would break strict-key export validation or be silently dropped from exports and replays
findings.evidence: The AI item object is validated with the exact keys ["criterionId","status","explanation","citations","ruleEvidenceIds"] (line 184), and risks are validated with the exact keys ["title","explanation","suggestion","citations"] (line 191). The export assessment envelope is allowlisted to ["id","deliveryId","method","mode","model","assessedAt","items","risks","limitations","coverage","usage"] (line 176). dataShapes does not inspect assessment items. The plan adds server-owned evidenceNeed (with reason and bounded targetFiles) to insufficient items (round 16) and quarantine metadata or a status-adjustment reason to risks (round 17). If these are written as new keys on ProofAssessmentItem or ProofAssessmentRisk, object() in the export rejects them as unsupported fields and createEvidenceExport fails. If they are stored outside the risk object, the existing zip of report.risks, task.source.riskIndex and task.source.risk (line 279) and SNAPSHOT_KEYS (line 29) do not retain them, so the export loses the receipt details the plan relies on. The same allowlists in dataShapes run on import, so older module copies that do not yet know the keys also reject newer exports.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: (1) an assessment with status insufficient_evidence saved with an added evidenceNeed field; (2) call createEvidenceExport, which reaches verifyEvidenceExport → check('ai-source-citations') → assessment() → object(item, [criterionId,status,explanation,citations,ruleEvidenceIds]) at line 184; (3) Object.keys contains evidenceNeed, so every() fails and requireValue throws; (4) createEvidenceExport line 153 throws 'This record cannot produce a consistent versioned evidence export'. The optional field is therefore not backward compatible for export. If the metadata is kept only in a side object, it does not reach the export at all.
findings.suggestion: In round 16, update assessment() line 184 and the risk loop line 191 to accept evidenceNeed (exact keys reason, targetFiles) and round 17's retained-risk keys with strict inner validation. Keep both optional, and add a verifier check that evidenceNeed.reason is in the server enum and that targetFiles is a subset of delivery.files with type html or css. Add a verification check id (for example evidence-need-bindings) that recomputes which items must be insufficient from the saved guard outputs and compares. Extend DELIVERY_KEYS and SNAPSHOT_KEYS only if the metadata is stored at the delivery or snapshot level. Decode an older export without the key as absent, not invalid. Include a budget note: the 30,000-unit report limit (delivery-assessment.ts line 252) is measured before these fields are added, so bound total evidenceNeed text so it cannot break previously valid reports.

findings.title: Round 16 reason assignment must be wired into the actual guard branches, not inferred after the fact, and old reports without metadata must stay truthful
findings.evidence: Status adjustments happen inside the item map at multiple separate branches: rule fail (271–273), requires_observation (274–276), article-title comma (278–284), business unknown/mismatch (286–308), exact copy (310–315), label coverage (317–322), universal tag (324–328), universal list (330–334) and empty citations (336–338). The unchanged generic branch sets status and explanation directly. originalStatuses are captured only from the raw wire response (line 364) and passed to publishSourceAssessmentNotes (line 365–367), which only receives the adjusted items, not the guard that caused each change. The plan requires the reason to come from the actual guard and never from regex over model prose, with a generic fallback when the model abstained. As written, the plan contains no recorded cause per status change. A later derivation from explanation text is exactly the forbidden regex path. The plan's claim that a missing old evidenceNeed is truthful is also unspecified: older stored assessments have no evidenceNeed, and a UI or export that renders 'next check' generically would imply the guard produced it.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: (1) the provider model returns supported for criterion c1; (2) labelCitationCheck returns incomplete, so line 320 sets status insufficient_evidence and explanation labelCitationCoverageExplanation; (3) the model also abstained on c2 with its own insufficient_evidence prose; (4) both items are insufficient_evidence, but the guard origin is lost once the map returns. A round-16 post-pass over items cannot tell label-coverage insufficiency from model abstention without reading prose. For older reports without evidenceNeed, a UI that shows evidenceNeed.nextCheck would show nothing or a synthesized target, which is not 'truthful'.
findings.suggestion: Return the cause from the mapping function itself. For example, each guard branch sets a local const cause = {reason:'label_coverage', targetFiles:[...]} next to the status assignment, and the return at line 341 includes evidenceNeed only for insufficient_evidence items. If no guard set a cause and the model returned insufficient_evidence, emit reason 'model_abstained' with no targetFiles and a fixed server fallback text. Never parse explanation. Keep evidenceNeed a function of the pipeline, not of post-hoc string matching. For old stored reports, make evidenceNeed optional and have the UI show an explicit 'not recorded in this report version' state rather than generating a next check. Round 18 should then add a negative test that strips evidenceNeed from an old-shape report and checks that export and UI still pass without inventing one.

findings.title: Round 17 quarantine cannot be rebuilt or verified from the export: the withheld count is prose-only, and the adjustment reason is lost on status-adjusted reports
findings.evidence: Line 38 returns {"risks":[]} whenever statusAdjustedCount > 0. Line 36 only writes the counts ('${statusAdjustedCount} item status(es) were adjusted ... ${risks.length} unreviewed optional AI risk(s) are temporarily withheld') into a free-text limitation string. The raw candidate risks are discarded before the report is returned, and line 382 stores only publication.risks. The export verifier therefore has no server field that records which risks were withheld or why, and no status-adjustment reason beyond a localized English or Chinese sentence. The plan's round 17 ('separate retained validated quarantinedRisks with explicit status-adjustment reason, never concatenated into active risks') is aimed at exactly this. It is also in tension with the plan to keep the report shape as a backward-compatible optional metadata addition: adding quarantinedRisks to ProofAssessment is a new top-level report key, and the export envelope at line 176 would reject it until it is added. A regex over limitation text (for example matching /withheld/) is fragile because the text is bilingual and not machine-replayable.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: (1) the model returns 2 risks and one guarded status adjustment; (2) publishSourceAssessmentNotes returns risks:[] and one limitation string; (3) createEvidenceExport runs assessment() on the saved report, which only validates items/risks/limitations; (4) verifyEvidenceExport has no check that could confirm '2 candidate risks were quarantined for reason X' or replay a status adjustment. The AgentReceipt-style replayable receipt cannot be checked offline. With statusAdjustedCount === 0, line 43 returns risks without quarantine fields, so the two branches already have different shapes for the same report type.
findings.suggestion: Add an optional, server-populated field on ProofAssessment (for example quarantinedRisks: {reason, risks}[] or statusAdjustments: {criterionId, guardReason}[]) with a strict shape. Keep risks as the active list only, never concatenated and never rewritten into limitations. Keep the field empty or absent when there is no quarantine so old payloads validate. Extend the export envelope allowlist at line 176 and add a verifier check that replays the publication policy and confirms that active and quarantined risks match the raw candidate count and adjustment reasons. Have round 18 add negative tests for a quarantined risk that is also present in active risks, and for an adjustment recorded with the wrong criterionId.

findings.title: 1000-unit draft budget is computed from a placeholder compose whose length can differ from the emitted text, and the truncated draft can drop the evidenceNeed next check
findings.evidence: Line 34 estimates overhead with compose('', '', true, true). The emitted text is compose(sourceText, explanationText, ...). This is only safe if every segment is a constant plus sourceText plus explanationText. That holds today. However, round 16 adds the server-owned evidenceNeed next check to the draft. If the next-check text is concatenated after the budget is computed, or if next-check content varies with targetFiles, line 34's overhead is wrong and the returned comment can exceed ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_MAX_UTF16, which is the existing feedback field limit. The 65/35 split (line 35) also always cuts the explanation first when the source is long. An insufficient_evidence item therefore loses its guard explanation excerpt exactly when the actionable next check matters most. targetFiles are also not included in the draft at all, so the seller gets no concrete files to address.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace with round 16 applied: criterion source length 2,900 and explanation length 590, with a 100-character next check that includes two targetFiles paths. The 1000-unit budget is consumed by the source first, and explanationText becomes empty or a short prefix. The comment stays under 1000 only if the next check was included in the line-34 placeholder; otherwise, the extra length overflows the contract limit. The final draft then says 'Please provide verifiable delivery evidence' with no mention of app/page.html.
findings.suggestion: Build the insufficient branch from structured parts: fixed intro, a server-generated next check that lists targetFiles from evidenceNeed.targetFiles, a bounded source excerpt and a bounded explanation excerpt. Compute the budget from the actual assembled string. Measure the assembled output in UTF-16 units, using the same astral-safe prefix already used, and assert length <= 1000 before return. When the draft is truncated, make sure an explicit 'excerpt' label covers the next check and that target files are never cut mid-path without a visible marker.

findings.title: Source-file targets for evidenceNeed will be validated against the post-validation file map, and the plan does not say how they are chosen or bounded
findings.evidence: Line 158 computes files = validateStaticFiles(delivery.files). Lines 159–194 and the guards use sent (html and css only) and files (all types). saveBusinessSteps, exactCopyCheck, labelCitationCheck, universalTagCheck and universalListCheck all operate on sent. Only line 153 checks bound item.file from rule evidence (length 300, CONTROL). The plan says insufficient items carry bounded targetFiles, but it does not specify: which file-kind set is allowed (raster paths never enter sent and cannot be cited), whether paths must also appear in coverage.includedFiles, how the path is bounded (UTF-16 length versus the 256 KiB path limit STATIC_RESOURCE_LIMITS.maxPathLength used at line 92), or whether an unknown or omitted target yields an empty list rather than a generic path. If the model, or any persisted old data, can supply targetFiles, a non-server path could reach the UI and the export. Any file outside files would make the export cite a missing file.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: (1) a guard (for example universalListCheck) fires because a required literal is missing on a specified page; (2) the plan maps this to a targetFiles value that has not been defined; (3) if the implementation derives the value from a criterion source or page alias rather than from quote.proof.project.requiredPages mapped through the saved spec, the path may be a bare filename such as 'menu.html' instead of the validated key (case and directory mismatches count as different keys); (4) a later export assessment() check (line 180) requires Object.hasOwn(delivery.files, file), so the feedback draft or export would reference a missing file, or the verifier would reject the export.
findings.suggestion: Define targetFiles as an ordered, deduplicated list of at most N paths, each drawn only from keys of sent or coverage.includedFiles, checked with a max length no larger than STATIC_RESOURCE_LIMITS.maxPathLength and with CONTROL rejected. A guard that cannot resolve a concrete file should emit an empty list plus ownReason 'no_target' rather than a guessed path. Round 18 should add negative tests where targetFiles contains an omitted raster, an unknown path, a path with a control character, or a list longer than N. These tests should assert that export and the UI degrade to the generic fallback, not fail export.

findings.title: Round 18 namespacing of manual review is not grounded in the criterion ID space, and manual-* reasoning already depends on a prefix convention
findings.evidence: Line 80 shows the three status values, and lines 143/145 show acceptanceEvidence manualChecks as string[]. The existing contracts label criterion identity via IDENTIFIER = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$/ (delivery-assessment.ts line 25). The prompt already special-cases ID prefixes: 'A criterion ID beginning manual-* or coverage-*' (line 186) and 'For manual-* and coverage-* criteria' (line 200). The plan's round 18 requires 'namespaced manual review'. As written, it does not define what the namespace keys on and whether legacy criterion IDs without a namespace remain valid. Two failure modes follow. First, prefix dispatch over prompt text is advice to the model, not an enforced boundary; a criterion with an ID that collides with the reserved namespace could be treated as human-only or, conversely, as source-checkable. Second, an export or history that already uses bare manual-* IDs (line 352 requires delivery.evidence needs_human rows to be inside snapshot.manualChecks) would need a migration or dual-read rule. Otherwise, round 18 negative tests would pass for new records and fail to protect historical ones.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: (1) a buyer confirms a criterion whose ID is 'manual-' + something that does not match the intended namespace form; (2) the report prompt at line 186/200 treats it as a manual criterion through prefix matching, while the round-18 namespace check treats it as an unknown namespace; (3) the two paths disagree about whether insufficient_evidence is mandatory for the item; (4) an export of a historical acceptance snapshot with the same ID passes the line-352 manualChecks check but fails the new namespace check.
findings.suggestion: Define the namespace as an explicit enum (for example manual: and coverage:), each mapped to a fixed server guard. Reserve those prefixes: when the buyer is about to lock a criterion, reject or rename colliding IDs. Keep a versioned migration or dual-read path for legacy IDs in history and exports, and make round 18 test both the new reserved IDs and the legacy bare IDs against the same verifier. Treat namespacing as a server validation rule, not only as prompt text.

findings.title: New plan fields have no version bump, so the named verifier rules identifier would overclaim what an old verifier checked
findings.evidence: EVIDENCE_EXPORT_SCHEMA is 'proofbeforepay-evidence-export-v1' (line 25), and SNAPSHOT_KEYS/DELIVERY_KEYS are frozen allowlists (lines 28–29). An optional server metadata field added to assessment items or risks (round 16/17) does not by itself change these constants. A verifier built before round 16 will run line 176/184 allowlists and either reject new reports or ignore the new metadata while still reporting consistency for EVIDENCE_EXPORT_RULES = 'pbp-static-source-v2'. An exported receipt would then assert a stronger evidenceNeed and quarantine replay than the rules identifier actually guarantees.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: (1) a receipt exported by a post-round-16 server is verified by a verifier that predates the new checks; (2) the verifier accepts v1/v2, ignores evidenceNeed, and returns consistency 'consistent' with a check set that has no evidence-need-bindings check; (3) the receipt claims a replayable evidenceNeed that was never checked.
findings.suggestion: Either bump EVIDENCE_EXPORT_RULES when the check set for assessment metadata changes, or add an explicit optional rulesVersion or check-set capability field that the verifier reports in checks[]. State in the verification message which checks ran. Round 18 should add a negative test that verifies a post-change export under the old rules identifier and expects unsupported or a different result.
